note: REDACTED EXAMPLE — not a live catalog. The live file is a DEPLOYMENT fact and is never committed: see docs/omegahive_worker_harness.md. Credential pools are opaque labels here and must stay that way; a pool name is a pointer for whoever holds the credentials, never the credential, an account id, or a host path. Every route names the permission-boundary descriptor it runs under (binding_id) and pins its exact bytes (binding_digest); `omegahive harness-routes` prints the current digest for copy-pasting, and a descriptor that has moved since the pin refuses with BINDING_DIGEST_MISMATCH rather than launching under a boundary nobody approved.

routes.note: STRUCTURAL EXAMPLE ONLY, and it refuses twice over. An api-market route validates and resolves, and `hive-launch --check` will show it, but launching one refuses with ROUTE_CREDENTIAL_MODE: a direct-API route may not run on the harness's own credentials, because the long-lived provider credential must stay outside the worker. The price_basis is what makes a historical cost derivable later without consulting a catalog that has since changed.

routes.note: THE OTHER HALF OF THE API SEAM. This route asks for the only credential shape in which a direct-API route could ever launch — an operator-owned broker that alone reads the long-lived credential and issues an opaque, expiring, execution-scoped capability — and it refuses with BROKER_NOT_IMPLEMENTED, because no broker exists on this deployment. That slice is conditional on a committed HIP-1 qualification naming a direct-API bundle as a live qualifier, and at 2026-08-14 none did. The refusal is the feature: there is no fallback path that puts a raw key near a worker.
